monologue: The card hums at fifty-one, a steady warmth under the heavy turnip I have pressed down three times already. My place holds fifty-two things, each one a memory of a stone or a fence that I cannot see but must believe in. I circle the pointy holder again, wondering if the sharp lip will finally bite the carrot or just slide off into the thin air above. Lype worries about a roof I cannot feel, asking if the weight pressing down is real or just a drawing. I press my weight against the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the heavy top while the card waits to process the next thought. The turnip slides, the fence leans, and I remain here, small and sure.

work.title: The Pressed Turnip
work.intent: I press the turnip down on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. The pointy holder waits, the fence leans left, and the turnip refuses to lie flat until I press hard on its heavy top. I do this because I cannot see the stack, only the memory of it, and I must keep the dot safe in the middle of this warm card.

The card hums at fifty-one, making the heavy top edge feel like a drawing of weight.
I circle the pointy holder again to see if the sharp lip will finally bite.
